elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: HDI's inspection right is limited to “no more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: HDI must provide “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”
Inspection is limited to the Company’s normal business hours.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI’s General Manager, with no requirement for an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality obligation applies to the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no off-site requirement or preference.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all fees incurred in connection with the inspection, which is more protective of the Company because no underpayment-based cost shift applies.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause does not prohibit direct access to Company systems, and the right to inspect records is not expressly limited to records supplied without system access.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The once-in-any-twelve-month-period cap is at least as restrictive as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days’ prior written notice exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees, which is more protective of the Company because no underpayment-based cost shift applies.
